claim: Overtime beyond normal daily hours must be paid at no less than 1.5 times the hourly rate of pay, however the pay is fixed (s.60A(3)(a)).
quote: For any overtime work carried out in excess of the normal hours of work, the employee shall be paid at a rate not less than one and half times his hourly rate of pay irrespective of the basis on which his rate of pay is fixed.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Overtime means hours worked beyond the normal hours per day; any work after the 10-hour spread-over period counts entirely as overtime (s.60A(3)(b)).
quote: In this section "overtime" means the number of hours of work carried out in excess of the normal hours of work per day
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A worker may not be required under the contract to work more than 8 hours a day, more than a 10-hour spread-over, or more than 45 hours a week, or more than 5 hours without a break of at least 30 minutes (s.60A(1)).
quote: more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes duration; (b) more than eight hours in one day; (c) in excess of a spread over period of ten hours in one day; (d) more than forty-five hours in one week
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Except in emergencies listed in s.60A(2)(a)-(e), no employer may require any employee to work more than 12 hours in one day (s.60A(7)).
quote: no employer shall require any employee under any circumstances to work for more than twelve hours in any one day
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The overtime limit is set by the Minister in regulations, not in the Act itself (s.60A(4)(a)); the number is not in this file.
quote: No employer shall require or permit an employee to work overtime exceeding such limit as may be prescribed by the Minister from time to time by regulations made under this Act
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Hours of work means time when the employee is at the employer's disposal and not free to dispose of his own time and movements (s.60A(9)).
quote: "hours of work" means the time during which an employee is at the disposal of the employer and is not free to dispose of his own time and movements
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: For a monthly-paid worker the ordinary daily rate of pay is the monthly rate divided by 26; the hourly rate is the ordinary rate divided by normal hours (s.60I).
quote: "hourly rate of pay" means the ordinary rate of pay divided by the normal hours of work
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Formula for a monthly-paid worker's ordinary rate of pay: monthly rate of pay divided by 26 (s.60I(1A)).
quote: Where an employee is employed on a monthly rate of pay, the ordinary rate of pay shall be calculated according to the following formula: monthly rate of pay . 26
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Every employee gets one whole rest day each week, set by the employer (s.59(1)).
quote: Every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as may be determined from time to time by the employer
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: No employee can be compelled to work on a rest day unless the work needs continuous shifts, except in the emergencies listed in s.60A(2) (s.60(1)).
quote: no employee shall be compelled to work on a rest day unless he is engaged in work which by reason of its nature requires to be carried on continuously or continually by two or more shifts
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Daily- or hourly-paid worker working on a rest day: up to half the normal hours = one day's wages; more than half up to normal hours = two days' wages (s.60(3)(a)).
quote: which does not exceed half his normal hours of work, one day's wages at the ordinary rate of pay; or (ii) which is more than half but does not exceed his normal hours of work, two days' wages at the ordinary rate of pay.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Monthly- or weekly-paid worker working on a rest day: up to half the normal hours = half a day's ordinary pay; more than half up to normal hours = one day's wages, on top of the monthly wage (s.60(3)(b)).
quote: which does not exceed half his normal hours of work, wages equivalent to half the ordinary rate of pay for work done on that day; or
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Work beyond normal hours on a rest day must be paid at no less than 2 times the hourly rate (s.60(3)(c)); piece-rated workers get twice the piece rate on a rest day (s.60(3)(d)).
quote: For any work carried out in excess of the normal hours of work on a rest day by an employee mentioned in paragraph (a) or (b), he shall be paid at a rate which is not less than two times his hourly rate of pay.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Every employee is entitled to a paid holiday on 11 gazetted public holidays a year, five of which must be National Day, the King's Birthday, the state Ruler's Birthday (or Federal Territory Day), Workers' Day and Malaysia Day (s.60D(1)(a)).
quote: on eleven of the gazetted public holidays, five of which shall be-- (i) the National Day; (ii) the Birthday of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong;
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The five fixed paid holidays include Workers' Day and Malaysia Day; employees also get any day appointed a public holiday for that year under s.8 of the Holidays Act 1951 (s.60D(1)(a)(iv)-(v), (b)).
quote: (iv) the Workers' Day; and (v) Malaysia Day; and (b) on any day appointed as a public holiday for that particular year under section 8 of the Holidays Act 1951
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: If a public holiday falls on a rest day or another public holiday, the next working day is a paid holiday instead (s.60D(1) proviso).
quote: the working day following immediately the rest day or the other public holiday shall be a paid holiday in substitution of the first mentioned public holiday
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The employer must display before each year a notice naming the remaining six gazetted holidays the workers will get (s.60D(1A)).
quote: a notice specifying the remaining six gazetted public holidays provided for in paragraph (1)(a)
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A worker who is absent without consent on the working day just before or after a public holiday loses holiday pay unless he has a reasonable excuse (s.60D(2)).
quote: shall not be entitled to any holiday pay for such holiday or consecutive holidays unless he has a reasonable excuse for such absence
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A worker required to work on a paid public holiday gets two days' wages at the ordinary rate in addition to the holiday pay, even if he works less than normal hours (s.60D(3)(a)).
quote: in addition to the holiday pay he is entitled to for that day-- (i) in the case of an employee employed on a monthly, weekly, daily, hourly, or other similar rate of pay, be paid two days' wages at the ordinary rate of pay;
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Overtime beyond normal hours on a paid public holiday must be paid at no less than 3 times the hourly rate (s.60D(3)(aa)).
quote: For any overtime work carried out by an employee referred to in subparagraph (a)(i) in excess of the normal hours of work on a paid public holiday, the employee shall be paid at a rate which is not less than three times his hourly rate of pay.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Paid annual leave: 8 days a year with under 2 years' service, 12 days with 2-5 years, 16 days with 5 years or more (s.60E(1)).
quote: eight days for every twelve months of continuous service with the same employer if he has been employed by that employer for a period of less than two years
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: If the contract ends before annual leave is taken, the employer must pay the ordinary rate for each untaken day, unless the worker was dismissed for misconduct (s.60E(3A)).
quote: the employer shall pay the employee his ordinary rate of pay in respect of every day of such leave
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Paid sick leave without hospitalisation: 14 days a year (under 2 years' service), 18 days (2-5 years), 22 days (5+ years); plus up to 60 days if hospitalisation is needed; examination at the employer's expense (s.60F(1)).
quote: of fourteen days in the aggregate in each calendar year if the employee has been employed for less than two years
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Up to 60 days' paid sick leave a year where hospitalisation is necessary (s.60F(1)(bb)).
quote: of sixty days in the aggregate in each calendar year if hospitalization is necessary
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Sick leave not certified by a doctor, or not reported to the employer within 48 hours, counts as absence without permission (s.60F(2)).
quote: without informing or attempting to inform his employer of such sick leave within forty-eight hours of the commencement thereof
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Maternity leave is at least 98 consecutive days (s.37(1)(d)(ii)).
quote: "eligible period" means a period of maternity leave of not less than *ninety-eight consecutive days
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A married male employee gets 7 consecutive days' paid paternity leave per birth, up to 5 births, if employed 12 months by the same employer and he notifies the employer (s.60FA).
quote: a married male employee shall be entitled to a paid paternity leave at his ordinary rate of pay for a period of seven consecutive days in respect of each confinement
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The contract must set a wage period of no more than one month; if none is set it is one month (s.18).
quote: A contract of service shall specify a wage period not exceeding one month.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Wages must be paid no later than the 7th day after the end of each wage period (s.19(1)).
quote: every employer shall pay to each of his employees not later than the seventh day after the last day of any wage period the wages, less lawful deductions earned by such employee during such wage period
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Pay for rest-day work, public-holiday work and overtime must be paid by the last day of the next wage period (s.19(2)).
quote: shall be paid not later than the last day of the next wage period
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The Director General of Labour may extend the time for paying wages on the employer's application if payment on time is not reasonably practicable (s.19(3)).
quote: he may, on the application of the employer, extend the time of payment by such number of days as he thinks fit
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: When a contract ends normally (end of term or with notice), unpaid wages must be paid no later than the day it ends (s.20).
quote: shall be paid to such employee not later than the day on which such contract of service so terminates
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: If the worker ends the contract without notice under s.13 or s.14(3), the employer must pay wages earned no later than the third day after termination (s.21(2)).
quote: shall be paid by the employer to the employee not later than the third day after the day on which the contract of service is so terminated
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: All wages less lawful deductions must be paid into a financial-institution account in the employee's name (or a joint account he chooses) (s.25(1)).
quote: shall be actually paid to him through payment into an account opened by a financial institution, being an account in the name of the employee
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A worker may recover in the courts any wages not paid into the account as required (s.25(2)).
quote: Every employee shall be entitled to recover in the courts so much of his wages, exclusive of sums lawfully deducted under Part IV, as shall not have been actually paid to him
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Cash or cheque payment is allowed only on the worker's written request and with the Director General's approval; the worker can withdraw the request with 4 weeks' written notice (s.25A).
quote: The employer shall, upon the written request of his employee under subsection (1), obtain approval from the Director General for the payment of wages to be paid in legal tender or by cheque.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: JTKSM FAQ: since the 2022 amendment, wages may be paid by cheque or cash only at the worker's written request and with the JTKSM Director General's permission.
quote: pembayaran gaji melalui cek atau tunai hanya dibenarkan atas permintaan bertulis pekerja kepada majikan dan dengan kebenaran daripada Ketua Pengarah JTKSM
note: JTKSM FAQ page footer shows 'Tarikh Kemaskini: 2 April 2026' (same day as the Wayback capture, may be a site-wide footer); content is about the 2022 amendments in force 1 Jan 2023; lead's note: footer date equals capture date, treated as site-wide, so undated

claim: An employer may not dictate where, how or with whom a worker spends his wages; any such contract term is void (s.26).
quote: No employer shall impose any condition in any contract of service as to the place at which, or the manner in which, or the person with whom, any wages paid to the employee are to be expended
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: An employer may not charge interest or discount on advances of up to one month's wages (s.27).
quote: from any employee by way of discount, interest or any similar charge on account of any advance or advances of wages
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: An employer who fails to pay wages within the times in ss.19-21, or deducts other than as allowed by s.24, commits an offence (s.91).
quote: makes deductions from the wages of an employee other than such deductions as are authorized by section 24
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: An employer who fails to pay wages under Part III is deemed to have broken the contract (s.15(1)).
quote: An employer shall be deemed to have broken his contract of service with the employee if he fails to pay wages in accordance with Part III.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A worker continuously absent more than two consecutive working days without leave or a reasonable excuse communicated to the employer is deemed to have broken the contract (s.15(2)).
quote: if he has been continuously absent from work for more than two consecutive working days without prior leave from his employer
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Wages for a partial month are monthly wages divided by days in the wage period times days eligible (s.18A).
quote: Calculation of wages for incomplete month's work
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: An employer may make no deductions from wages except as the Employment Act allows (s.24(1)).
quote: No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Deductions allowed without the worker's request: overpayment by mistake in the previous 3 months, indemnity for leaving without notice, interest-free wage advances, and deductions authorised by any other written law (s.24(2)).
quote: deductions to the extent of any overpayment of wages made during the immediately preceding three months
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: s.24(2)(d): deductions authorised by any other written law are lawful.
quote: (d) deductions authorized by any other written law.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: s.24(4)(c) and (e): deductions for payments to a third party, and for accommodation rent, services, food and meals provided by the employer, need written request plus Director General permission.
quote: deductions in respect of payments to a third party on behalf of the employee
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: s.24(4)(e): rent for accommodation and the cost of services, food and meals provided by the employer are deductible only with written request and DG permission.
quote: deductions in respect of the rental for accommodation and the cost of services, food and meals provided by the employer to the employee at the employee's request or under the terms of the employee's contract of service
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The Director General may not allow accommodation or food deductions unless satisfied they benefit the worker (s.24(5)).
quote: The Director General shall not permit any deduction for payments under paragraph (4)(e) unless he is satisfied that the provision of the accommodation, services, food or meals is for the benefit of the employee.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Total deductions in any month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned that month (s.24(8)), except deductions from final pay on termination, indemnity, and approved housing-loan repayments (s.24(9)).
quote: The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: The 50% limit does not apply to deductions from the final wage payment for amounts the worker owes the employer at termination (s.24(9)(b)).
quote: deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee's contract of service
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Unless the written contract says otherwise, notice to end a contract must be equal for both sides and at least 4 weeks (under 2 years' service), 6 weeks (2-5 years) or 8 weeks (5+ years); notice must be written (s.12).
quote: four weeks' notice if the employee has been so employed for less than two years on the date on which the notice is given
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Either side may end the contract without notice by paying the wages for the notice period (indemnity) (s.13(1)); either side may end it without notice for a wilful breach by the other (s.13(2)).
quote: Either party to a contract of service may terminate such contract of service without notice in the event of any wilful breach by the other party of a condition of the contract of service.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: An employer may dismiss for misconduct only after due inquiry; during the inquiry suspension is at most 2 weeks on at least half pay (s.14(1)-(2)).
quote: An employer may, on the grounds of misconduct inconsistent with the fulfilment of the express or implied conditions of his service, after due inquiry
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: A worker may leave without notice if he or his dependants are immediately threatened by violence or disease he did not agree to risk (s.14(3)).
quote: An employee may terminate his contract of service with his employer without notice where he or his dependants are immediately threatened by danger to the person by violence or disease
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: Termination, lay-off and retirement benefits are set by Ministerial regulations under s.60J; the rates are not in the Act.
quote: The Minister may, by regulations made under this Act, provide for the entitlement of employees to, and for the payment by employers of-- (a) termination benefits; (b) lay-off benefits; (c) retirement benefits.
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked

claim: In a redundancy, the employer may not retrench a local worker until all foreign workers in a similar job have been terminated (s.60N).
quote: the employer shall not terminate the services of a local employee unless he has first terminated the services of all foreign employees employed by him in a capacity similar to that of the local employee
note: Employment Act 1955 updated text as at 1 Jan 2023 (latest amendment Act A1651); applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; later amendments not checked
